title: Object Safety and Trait Objects
goal: Learn why some traits cannot be turned into dyn Trait objects.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 3 Afternoon: dyn Trait

sections.text: In Java or C++, any interface can be used as a reference type. In Rust, `dyn Trait` requires the trait to be object-safe.

A trait is object-safe when all its methods can be placed in a single vtable. If a method returns `Self` or uses generic type parameters, the compiler cannot build a vtable because sizes depend on the concrete caller.
When code attempts to build `dyn Duplicable`, Rust rejects it with error `E0038`. Use generics `T: Duplicable` instead when methods return `Self`.
Dynamic dispatch trades monomorphized speed for runtime vtable lookup, but only for traits where method signatures are fixed and type-erased.

explanation: Learn why some traits cannot be turned into dyn Trait objects.
